title: Runtime hotpatch prober for attention kernels and safety metrics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight runtime "hotpatch" prober that can inject and evaluate micro-updates to attention kernel selection heuristics (FlashAttention v2/v3 candidates and quantized variants) without a full runtime rollout. Collect a compact safety metrics set (latency distribution deltas, memory fragmentation, KV cache hit variance, and correctness diffs on a sampled prompt set) to allow safe, fast iteration on selection heuristics and emergency rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch channel: can push a JSON heuristic bundle to a single staging pod and have it applied within 30s
Metrics: new safety metrics (p50/p95 latency delta, mem-frag-index, kv-hit-delta, token-error-rate) are emitted to the perf dashboard and stored for 72h
Rollout gating: Automated rollback runs when p95 latency increases >10% or mem-frag-index > 0.12 for 15 minutes
Canary: ability to target 1%, 10%, 50% traffic splits for canary experiments with consistent routing and telemetry
No user-visible correctness regressions on the golden prompt set (0 tolerance for top-1 token divergence on validation prompts)
implementation_notes: Design hotpatch format: small JSON containing kernel candidate list, score weights, memory-safety thresholds, and warmup policy. Keep size <10KB.
Runtime apply: implement a non-blocking updater that swaps heuristic without restarting runtime threads; change is atomic per worker thread group.
Prober harness: instrument a staged warmup that runs micro-benchmarks (short synthetic sequences) to verify kernel selection under low-latency constraints before enabling on live traffic.
Telemetry: emit a compact 'hotpatch-safety' event with delta metrics and patch id; wire to existing perf pipeline and add a lightweight Grafana overview for quick triage.
Safety thresholds: configurable per-patch; default conservative values to avoid regressions on p95 and memory usage.
Compatibility: support FlashAttention v2/v3 flags, quantized kernels (int8/4-bit) and arch-specific kernel blacklists.
Fallback mode: if the prober detects OOMs or correctness diffs it should revert locally and mark the patch as 'failed' with root-cause signals.
Chaos testing: add unit-level fault injection to emulate partial worker apply and network partition for the hotpatch endpoint.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hotpatch misconfiguration causes broad p95 regression. Mitigation: default to single-worker staging, conservative thresholds, immediate auto-revert trigger and alerting to on-call SRE.
Risk: Heuristic bundles abused for insecure configs. Mitigation: sign hotpatch bundles and require RBAC role to publish; reject unsigned patches.
Risk: Observability blind spots for memory fragmentation. Mitigation: add mem-frag-index metric (heap fragmentation normalized by active buffers) and correlate with OOM events.

Risk: Correctness diffs undetected for rare prompts. Mitigation: maintain a large, curated golden prompt set with stratified sampling across models and token lengths; enforce top-1 token equality in gating phase.
Risk: Cross-arch inconsistency (A100 vs H100). Mitigation: prober runs arch-specific microbenchmarks and applies kernel candidates conditional on detected GPU family.
